text:
sam: Heads up — us-west GPU pool (p4) is at sustained ~92% allocation this morning, we're seeing a spike in 429s on API keys. Dashboard: https://grafana.internal/redwood/us-west/p4

maria: what's our current per-org token-bucket sizing? static qps or capacity-aware?

sam: static right now. per-org bucket = min(100 qps, account_quota). clearly bad when capacity drops.

jeff: we should move to capacity-proportional refill. naive idea: refill = floor(available_gpu_slots * 100 / active_orgs). add smoothing to avoid oscillation during autoscale.

maria: +1. also want a burst allowance for short chat sessions — maybe bucket_size = refill_per_sec * 5 by default.

leah: active_orgs is noisy. use EWMA over 60s to stabilize counts.

sam: Proposed pseudo-algo: 
```
active = ewma(active_orgs, 60s)
refill_per_sec = max(1, floor((available_gpu_slots * tokens_per_gpu_per_sec) / max(1, active)))
burst = refill_per_sec * burst_window_seconds   # burst_window_seconds default 5
if node_pool_utilization > 0.85:
  refill_per_sec *= 0.5  # temporary backoff to prioritize reserved capacity
```
Also: reserved/contracted orgs should get guaranteed min_refill.

maria: how do we mark reserved keys? key metadata with tier field — reserved -> guaranteed_min_refill config.

jeff: proxy-level admission control idea: if proxy_queue_length > qlen_threshold, start soft-429ing low-priority keys or return 202 queued for async calls. we can implement a small enqueue service with queue_id + webhook when ready.

leah: region spill? if us-west is full, allow cross-region spill to us-east for orgs that opted in. add per-org routing policy. default: same-region only.

sam: agree. add opt-in flag in console. ops note: spilling increases egress and model cache warm-up costs. need cost estimate in UI.

maria: cost team: show estimated extra $ per 1k requests when cross-region spill is on.

jeff: full implementation plan:
- token-bucket service (keyed by org:key), supports dynamic refill hooks and tiered guarantees
- coordinator pulls scheduler metrics (available_gpus per pool) and publishes refill rates
- proxy enforces token consumption, supports enqueue with priority and soft-429 logic
- console: per-org controls (spill opt-in, min_guarantee, show cost delta)

leah: testing plan: staging with artificially capped available_gpus; run 100 org simulators with mixed bursty/steady traffic. also chaos: flapping capacity and observe oscillation.

sam: smoothing defaults: ewma alpha 0.2, burst_window 5s, scale_back_at_util 0.85. start conservative.

maria: UX question — when queued do we return 202 + queue_id or 429 + Retry-After? 202 allows async flow and webhooks; 429 simpler for sync callers.

jeff: dual-mode makes sense: async endpoints -> 202 queued (requires idempotency key), sync endpoints -> 429 + Retry-After. log metrics for both.

leah: can we hot-configure thresholds per-pool so we can try different aggressiveness in staging vs prod?

sam: yes. central config store (k8s configmap / consul) with rollout via console.

maria: quick thought on fairness: we may want token borrow between keys in same org (org-level bucket + per-key buckets). helps bursty single-key apps.

jeff: good point. hierarchy: org_bucket (guaranteed) + key_bucket (fair share). enforcement: consume key_bucket first, then org_bucket if available.

capacity-bot: NodePool us-west-p4: alloc 92%, avg latency 120ms, proxy_queue 110, active_orgs_est=184

sam: i'll prototype a local token-bucket service + coordinator and open a draft RFC/PR. will include a small simulator and sample metrics.

maria: thanks — please @eng-platform when PR is ready. :thumbsup:
